author: Speedway Digest Staff
title: Hendrick Motorsports, Joe Gibbs Racing Lead Title Fight Into Kansas - NewsBreak
text:
By Speedway Digest Staff ,
1 days ago KANSAS CITY, Kan. - The NASCAR Cup Series arrives at Kansas Speedway this weekend for the fourth race of the Chase, and several of the sport's powerhouse organizations enter the 1.5-mile oval carrying momentum and championship aspirations.
Few teams have been stronger at intermediate tracks than Kyle Larson and Hendrick Motorsports. Larson enters Kansas as the championship leader after finishing second at Bristol, extending his streak of top-five finishes in all three Chase races. He has won three times at Kansas, led more than 1,000 laps at the track and remains one of the favorites entering Sunday's Hollywood Casino 400.
"I definitely don't believe we're going to go to the next three racetracks and be the fastest car, but I think we'll be a top-five car," Larson said. "You can execute from there and score a lot of points or potentially have a shot to win."
Larson is not the only Hendrick driver with a strong Kansas résumé. Chase Elliott returns as the defending winner of the fall race and owns two victories at the speedway. William Byron has consistently produced results on intermediate tracks this season, while Alex Bowman has recorded 11 top-10 finishes at Kansas, more than at any other track in his career.
"Now is our time to shine," Byron said. "We're heading to tracks that are our bread and butter. We're not out yet."
Standing in the way of Hendrick's charge is Joe Gibbs Racing, which has amassed eight Cup Series victories at Kansas. Denny Hamlin enters the weekend second in the standings and remains tied with the track's best performers after collecting four career wins at the venue. Earlier this season, Hamlin led 131 laps before finishing fourth.
Teammates Christopher Bell, Ty Gibbs, and Chase Briscoe also arrive with championship hopes. Bell owns four poles at Kansas in the Next Gen era and sits fourth in the standings, while Gibbs continues a career season with two wins and a fifth-place position in points
Another Toyota organization expected to contend is 23XI Racing. The team has dominated at Kansas in recent years, producing victories from Kurt Busch, Bubba Wallace, and Tyler Reddick. Reddick won the spring race at Kansas and hopes to regain momentum after slipping to seventh in the Chase standings.
Kansas also marks the beginning of a critical three-race run on 1.5-mile tracks that includes Las Vegas and Charlotte.
"Getting back to these mile-and-a-half tracks gives us an opportunity to work on our overall package," Cody Ware said. "Kansas is a good way to kick off that stretch and build a baseline for the next few races."
